mandate.summary: The MBTA runs Greater Boston's public-transport network — subway, bus, commuter rail and the Boston Harbor ferries linking downtown to Charlestown, East Boston, the South Shore and North Shore, ticketed through the MBTA system.
current_priorities: Harbor and South/North Shore commuter ferry service
Integrating ferries into the MBTA network and fares
Electrifying the fleet under state climate law
Relieving the region's congested, flood-exposed land routes

policy_targets.vision: Massachusetts Clean Energy and Climate Plan 2050
policy_targets.decarb_note: Massachusetts law mandates net zero by 2050 and the MBTA has committed to fleet electrification — but the harbor ferries still run on diesel, and demand for the Hingham and inner-harbor lines keeps growing.
policy_targets.relevance: Navier is the zero-emission foiling upgrade to a network the MBTA already runs — faster harbor and South Shore commutes that relieve the expressway and tunnels while delivering the fleet electrification state law requires.

precedent.headline: Public harbor ferries are core MBTA commuter infrastructure, not a novelty.
precedent.network: The MBTA runs year-round and seasonal ferries (routes F1–F7) from Long Wharf and Rowes Wharf to Charlestown, East Boston, Hingham, Hull, Winthrop, Lynn and Quincy, integrated into the MBTA network.
precedent.note: Public ferry service is core transport infrastructure here, not a novelty. Navier adds a fast passenger-only foiling layer on the busy corridors.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier is the zero-emission foiling upgrade to a network the MBTA already runs — faster harbor and South Shore commutes that relieve the expressway and tunnels while delivering the fleet electrification state law requires.

domestic_network.note: Candidate boarding points with APPROXIMATE anchor coordinates [lng, lat] for Grok to snap to real piers/terminals during seal. Coordinates are anchors, not sealed geometry. Core mirrors the authority's live public stops; new/committed/study stops are flagged.

domestic_pairs.rationale: The year-round Charlestown Navy Yard commuter line.
The East Boston (Lewis Mall) inner-harbor line.
The flagship Hingham commuter line down the South Shore.
South Shore link between Hingham and Hull.
South Shore to airport via the harbor.
Hub-spoke: Long Wharf ↔ Rowes Wharf (orphan BP on published network)
Hub-spoke: Long Wharf ↔ Seaport (Fan Pier) (orphan BP on published network)

regional_links.note: Domestic-only network across Boston Harbor and the South/North Shore. Provincetown / Cape links are seasonal and secondary, out of scope for this phase.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every domestic leg must be routed through navigable open water with NO land crossings (interior_land_km == 0). Hand-curated waypoints required wherever a breakwater, barrier, bridge pier, reef, headland, naval/exclusion zone or shallows would otherwise be clipped. Use data-clean/uae_hand_waypoints.json format {from, to, waypoints:[[lng,lat]...]}.

hazards.detail: The main shipping channel and Logan approach are busy with container, cruise and tanker traffic — cross at marked points; coordinate with the Logan ferry dock.
Boston Harbor Islands and shoals (e.g. off Hull/Quincy) require hand-waypointing through the marked channels.
The Logan ferry dock sits inside the airport security perimeter — routing must respect the marine exclusion zones.
Hingham/Hull/Quincy approaches have tidal flats and narrow channels — follow the marked fairways at all tides.
